title: Rafael and the Ledger
premise: In the port town of Saltmere, 1897, Gideon Kavanagh — once a pearl diver's son, now an indentured clerk to the Meridian Trading Company — keeps the ledger that records every debt, wage, and indenture in the district. When imperial troops requisition the town and seize the company's records, Gideon discovers the ledger also contains proof that the company sold its indentured workers to the army as forced labor, his dead father's name among them. Copying the incriminating pages, he must carry them past three military checkpoints to a journalist in the capital before the original ledger is burned and the witnesses deported. He succeeds at the cost of his own indenture papers and near-certain arrest, ending the story free but nameless, watching the scandal break from a ship's deck with nothing left to carry but the truth.
about_author: L. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company records in Southeast Asian ports. Their fiction draws on the ledgers, manifests, and marginalia of people whose names survive only as entries in someone else's accounting.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A day in Saltmere's trading house: Gideon balances the ledger, records a diver's death as a line item, and remembers his father's drowning in the pearl beds. He measures his life in portable things — a habit from childhood. Emotional beat: quiet grief beneath routine, and the first hint that names in the ledger are treated as currency, not people.

chapters.title: Gunboats at the Harbor Mouth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The imperial army arrives, requisitions Saltmere, and orders the company to surrender all records. Manager Aldous Vane complies with suspicious eagerness, but Gideon notices Vane pocketing a single slim volume — the master ledger — before the soldiers inventory the rest. Emotional beat: dread and the dawning sense that the ledger matters more than anyone is saying.

chapters.title: What Vane Keeps in the Back Room
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Sent to fetch the ledger for a military auditor, Gideon glimpses the hidden pages: contracts selling indentured workers to the army as forced laborers, his father's name among them, marked 'deceased — asset closed.' He steals a look, memorizes nothing, but takes a rubbing. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Copyist's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with a scene from Sergeant Ilsa Rehn's perspective. Gideon begins copying the incriminating pages at night; Rehn, the checkpoint commander, suspects the trading house is hiding something and tightens inspections. Vane grows paranoid and begins watching his clerks. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension — the copy is nearly done, and so is the net closing.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Betrayal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A fellow clerk, Tomas, discovers the copies and, indebted to Vane, reports him. Gideon hides the pages inside a bundle of requisition receipts and escapes the trading house as soldiers search his quarters. Emotional beat: betrayal by the closest thing he had to a friend, and flight into the occupied streets.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Fish Gate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Disguised as a fish porter, Gideon passes the Fish Gate checkpoint by hiding the pages in a salted catch barrel, nearly undone when Rehn herself inspects the shipment. A diver's widow, Maren, vouches for him at cost to herself. Emotional beat: terror and the first taste of solidarity — he cannot carry this alone.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The River Toll
chapters.summary: Gideon and Maren's POV alternating. At the river toll, papers are checked against a new wanted list bearing Gideon's description. Maren's nephew, a soldier, waves them through out of family shame he cannot name. Vane arrives minutes behind them, offering a reward. Emotional beat: the corrupting reach of power — everyone has a price, and Gideon wonders about his own.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Capital Gate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final checkpoint demands full interrogation. Rehn is there, transferred ahead of them, and recognizes him. Instead of arresting him, she lets him pass — she has read the ledger's requisition orders and knows her own brother is listed among the 'laborers' sent to the mines. Emotional beat: the enemy's conscience as the story's hinge; mercy bought at Rehn's ruin.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Books
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, intercut with Saltmere. In the capital, Gideon delivers the pages to journalist Edith Calloway as soldiers burn the original ledger in Saltmere's square and deport the witnesses — including Tomas, who finally tells Vane nothing. Vane realizes the copy exists and that his empire of paper has failed. Emotional beat: grief for what burns, triumph for what survives.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The scandal breaks; Vane is arrested, but Gideon's own indenture papers burned with the ledger, leaving him legally nameless and free. He sails from the capital as Calloway's story runs, carrying only his father's pearl knife. Rehn, court-martialed, sends him a single line: 'Some debts forgive themselves.' Emotional beat: bittersweet liberation — freedom won by losing everything except the truth.
